call_points.text: Custom manufacturing revenue target of ₹1,000 Cr is about 12 months behind; management still expects to reach it next financial year.
The 7.5% PVC customs duty is expected to return at end of June, adding $60-70 to realisations.
Paste PVC: DGTR final findings received on EU and Japan imports; awaiting Finance Ministry notification, expected in first half of FY27.
Suspension PVC demand was about 1 percentage point below last year at 4.3 million tons; demand seen stable or marginally up.
Consolidated net debt stood at ₹1,419 Cr as of March 31, 2026.
Board formed a committee of three independent directors to examine strategic priorities, including reorganisation and M&A.
Analysts pressed on whether FY27 will also be stressful for CCVL; management said possible on a pessimistic view but sees Chinese producers under cost pressure.

timeline.summary: On 18 May 2026, Chemplast Sanmar commenced commercial production of R32 refrigerant gas at its swing plant in Mettur.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹1,255.55 Cr (+9.1% YoY), net loss ₹45.38 Cr (against a loss of ₹54.17 Cr a year earlier).
On May 25, 2026, Chemplast Sanmar released its Q4 & FY26 investor presentation, highlighting a Q4 revenue of ₹1,255.55 Cr and commencement of R32 production.
On 28 May 2026, Chemplast Sanmar commenced commercial production at Phase III of its Multi-Purpose Production Block III at Berigai.

On 26 May 2026, Chemplast Sanmar's Q4 & FY26 earnings call disclosed a ₹898 Cr standalone impairment on its CCVL investment, a ₹150 Cr exceptional charge at CCVL, and a board committee of three independent directors to examine strategic priorities including reorganisation and M&A.
